problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $A(5,-3,1)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨8,1,0⟩+s⟨3,2,5⟩$ and $r=⟨6,-5,10⟩+t⟨0,6,2⟩.$

feedback.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $E(16,-1,3)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨9,-7,2⟩+s⟨5,1,-2⟩$ and $r=⟨15,2,-3⟩+t⟨1,11,3⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨5,1,-2⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨1,11,3⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $E(16,-1,3)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $e=⟨16,-1,3⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =e+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨16,-1,3⟩+s⟨5,1,-2⟩+t⟨1,11,3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
